clue.text: Wardrobe assistant who's upset an ugly sister, perhaps?

parts.note: upset as in annoyed or angry, which is cross
a dresser is the theatre staff member who helps actors into their costumes

explanation.surface: A backstage helper in the costume department is annoyed with one of Cinderella's ugly sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pantomime the Ugly Sisters are traditionally played by men in drag; pantomime is a comic family stage show staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the pantomime role of an Ugly Sister is played by a man wearing women's clothes, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Flat switched with top housing, seeking small entrance

indicators.note: housing means the hat-word holds the jumbled letters within it

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen

indicators.note: switched means the letters of flat are swapped around into another order

explanation.surface: Someone swaps flats and moves into one with a top floor, looking for a small doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like a home, but it is just fodder; 'switched' gives TFLA, and 'housing' tucks it into the hat word.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a small hinged opening in a door lets a pet go in and out of the house.

clue.text: Outlaw was given weapon — that's something of a gamble

parts.note: someone who was given a weapon is one armed, read as 'one (who is) armed'
a bandit is an outlaw or robber

explanation.surface: A robber is handed a gun, and that is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: The ONE is loose: 'was given weapon' describes one who is armed, the bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fruit machine with a pull lever is a gambling device, so it is a form of betting.

clue.text: Ridiculous leaders in England and Scotland up for a battle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means ridiculously excessive

indicators.note: leaders in means the first letters of the two country names

explanation.surface: Absurd heads of the English and Scottish sides are ready for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns OTTES, all the pieces together, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brief fight or heated argument is a scrap or battle.

clue.text: Break something curved, so mend racket

parts.note: a rest is a break or pause
a ring is a curved shape

explanation.surface: Someone snaps a bent object and so has to repair a noisy fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like noise, but it is the tennis racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: putting new strings in a tennis racket repairs it after a string snaps.

clue.text: Problem over old slappers fighting?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A tricky situation with some old floozies having a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slappers' looks like British slang for loose women, but here it means wrestlers who slap each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: Japanese wrestlers push and slap at each other to force an opponent out of the ring.

clue.text: Dear old writers I have to support?

parts.note: ex means former, so old
pens are writing instruments
I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A letter writer wonders whether they must support some former writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like the opening of a letter, but it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something dear costs a lot of money.

clue.text: Weed pocketing undies makes inappropriate complaint to a servant?

indicators.note: pocketing means the garden tool word holds the scrambled letters within it

parts.note: to hoe is to weed a garden bed

indicators.note: inappropriate signals that the letters of undies makes are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs underwear into their pocket and complains improperly to a member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an ailment, not a grievance; 'inappropriate' gives USEMAIDSKNE, which the garden-tool word pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: knee inflammation from long kneeling was named after the scrubbing staff who suffered it, so it is an ailment of servants.

clue.text: One with an image of Darwin's sound character

definitions.text: One with an image of Darwin

indicators.note: sound means a word heard spoken that resembles another in pronunciation

parts.note: tenor means the general character or drift of something

explanation.surface: A sound, upright person happens to look like Charles Darwin.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Darwin appeared on the Bank of England ten-pound note from 2000 to 2018.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the British ten-pound note carried a portrait of the naturalist, so it is a banknote with his picture.

clue.text: Chirpy message?

parts.note: a short Twitter post, and a bird's chirp, both share this name

explanation.surface: A cheerful note.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a post on Twitter carries a bird's name for chirping, so a short online message that is also a chirp.

clue.text: Aggrieved about plan — what about it? It's flagging

indicators.note: about means the word for aggrieved surrounds the rest

parts.note: sore means aggrieved or resentful

indicators.note: about it means the questioning word goes around the word for plan

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
a map is a plan or chart

explanation.surface: Someone resentful about a scheme asks what it is all about, and their energy is waning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flagging' looks like tiring, but it means signalling with flags; 'what about it' is the questioning word wrapped round the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a signalling system using hand-held flags, so it is literally flag-waving communication.

clue.text: Fat swine's gone in for port

indicators.note: gone in means the pig word is placed inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
a boar is a male swine; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A greedy pig has gone in for some port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but it is the old word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an archaic sailing term for the left-hand side of a vessel.

clue.text: Concert's scheduled to happen after the middle of June

indicators.note: after means the central letters of the month come first, followed by the phrase
the middle of means the inner letters of the month name

parts.note: if an event is scheduled to happen it is on, as in 'the show is on'; the 's of Concert's gives IS

explanation.surface: A musical performance is booked for after mid-June.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Concert's' supplies IS, joining 'scheduled to happen' (ON).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: acting in concert means acting together, all as one voice.

clue.text: Important application of buttons?

definitions.meaning: pushing a button down is the act of applying pressure to it

explanation.surface: An urgent need to use buttons.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: urgent and important, or the act of pushing buttons.

clue.text: Promptly imbibing endless beer, outlaw in pub room

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for promptly holds the shortened beer

parts.note: soon means promptly or shortly

indicators.note: endless means the beer word loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
to bar is to outlaw or ban

explanation.surface: A bandit quickly drinking beer in a room of a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In older British pubs the saloon bar was the more comfortable lounge, separate from the public bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British pub was traditionally divided into rooms, the smarter one being the lounge or saloon.

clue.text: Lighting fixture not as smart?

definitions.meaning: a switch that lowers the brightness of a lamp

explanation.surface: A light switch that is not very clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a light-control switch, and the comparative of stupid, meaning less clever.

clue.text: Clue less hard with jumbo flipping complete!

indicators.note: less means the abbreviation for hard is taken away from the word for clue

parts.note: a hint is a clue
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: flipping means the letters of the jumbo word are tossed into a new order

parts.note: jumbo means large or enormous

explanation.surface: An exasperated solver finds a clue made easier by an elephant: absolutely flipping complete!
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath, but it rearranges the jumbo word into EGRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something integral is whole or complete.

clue.text: Nice support for a woman reversing charabanc

indicators.note: reversing means the coach word is turned backwards where it sits in the dress support

parts.note: a bustle was a pad worn to hold out the back of a woman's skirt
a charabanc is an old-fashioned motor coach, a bus

explanation.surface: A pleasant support for a woman backing a coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns the BUS at the start of BUSTLE into SUB. 'Nice' means finely discriminating, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nice distinction is a fine or delicate one.

clue.text: Verbal abuse about husband in comedy routine

indicators.note: about means the word for verbal abuse surrounds the letter for husband

parts.note: to give someone stick is to criticise them harshly

explanation.surface: A comedian's act full of insults about a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a comedian's gimmick or routine act.

clue.text: Lack of faith I feel bunkum, not half ludicrous

indicators.note: ludicrous signals the letters are thrown into an absurd new order
not half means only half of the nonsense word is kept

explanation.surface: A sceptic sees the nonsense as half ludicrous and so loses their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps BUN from BUNKUM; 'ludicrous' rearranges I FEEL + BUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: absence of religious belief or faith.

clue.text: Might one be wounded thus, as no slight adversary?

parts.note: not slight means fat
the 'no' carries over: no adversary is an ally

explanation.surface: A tough opponent might inflict a mortal wound.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'no' works twice: no slight one is FAT, and no adversary is an ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage: a mortal wound is inflicted in this manner, causing death.

clue.text: Beat that backing system for sound

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: backing means the word for that is turned around

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that

explanation.surface: Beat that backing track on the sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is a public-address loudspeaker system, the trade name used in Britain for any PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a British brand of public-address loudspeakers used in stations and stadiums.

clue.text: Stout cook's guzzled starter in vichyssoise? Unfortunately, yes

indicators.note: guzzled means the word for cook swallows the other letters

parts.note: to heat food is to cook it; the 's stands for has

indicators.note: starter in means the first letter of the soup
unfortunately signals the letters of yes come out in an unlucky order

explanation.surface: A portly chef has gulped down a cold leek soup, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Vichyssoise is a cold leek and potato soup; only its first letter is used. 'Unfortunately' gives YSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: thickset or stocky in build.

clue.text: Notable royal, poisonous type

parts.note: a VIP, very important person, is a notable
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A distinguished royal person is a venomous character.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an adder is a venomous snake, one poisonous kind.

clue.text: Rising star, runner

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming star sprinter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is the crossword sense of a river: the Avon is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword sense: a river runs, so it is a runner.

clue.text: Negotiate insurance, ringing branch

indicators.note: ringing means the word for insurance encircles the word for branch

parts.note: cover is insurance protection
a limb is a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: Bargaining over an insurance policy for a branch office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiate' means get over an obstacle, not bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to negotiate an obstacle such as a fence is to get over it.

clue.text: Board stolen apparently after turning over nails

indicators.note: turning over means the run of letters is read backwards
nails means grabs or holds, so the phrase holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: Planks apparently taken, after the thief turns over some nails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nails' pins a run inside 'stolen apparently': LENAP, which 'turning over' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a flat board or sheet forming part of a surface.

clue.text: Time perhaps for this matriarch to keep rocking cradle

indicators.note: to keep means the word for matriarch holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: a granny heads the family

indicators.note: rocking signals that the letters of cradle are moved about

explanation.surface: Time for granny to rock the baby's cradle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is a prison sentence, the punishment for serious theft; 'rocking' gives DLARCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: serious theft is a crime for which a prison sentence (doing time) may be given.
